source.title: Mildly Overparametrized Neural Nets can Memorize Training Data Efficiently
source.authors: Rong Ge; Run-Zhe Wang; Haoyu Zhao

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; some equations and symbols appear garbled by text extraction, but the main results and experiment descriptions are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The paper analyzes and experimentally trains networks to memorize arbitrary or random labels, using squared loss and polynomial activations rather than benchmark classification accuracy.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the paper's own theoretical training guarantees and reported experiments. CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 classification results are not reported; figures give no precise plotted values beyond the text descriptions. Results cited from Zhang et al. and other prior work are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study investigates memorization using fully connected polynomial-activation networks and squared regression loss on synthetic data and MNIST. V1 specifies convolutional networks reaching near-zero training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100. These results concern a related but different system and measure. The study does not test V2–V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly correct. The authors prove efficient memorization for particular two- and three-layer polynomial architectures under rank or smoothed-data conditions, using perturbed gradient descent with a small norm regularizer. Their parameter and neuron bounds match memorization-capacity bounds up to constants in the stated regimes. Experiments demonstrate synthetic regression fitting and MNIST scalar-label fitting with Adam, strongly affected by input perturbation. Extending the results to standard activations and proving generalization remain open.
record.recipe_differences: The results concern polynomial-activation networks trained with perturbed gradient descent in theory and Adam in MNIST experiments, using squared regression loss; the claim version describes convolutional classification benchmarks trained with SGD or Adam.
record.method_sensitivity: Input perturbation materially changes reported MNIST fit, especially for random labels; the paper also states learning-rate decay is crucial for high accuracy in the two-layer MNIST experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: The synthetic quadratic network rapidly reaches zero regression loss. On MNIST, the unperturbed two-layer model slows near loss 0.1 with original labels and fits random labels poorly; Gaussian input perturbation permits loss below 1e-5 with original labels and very accurate random-label fitting.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Quadratic networks can memorize synthetic and MNIST scalar targets through gradient-based regression training, with input conditioning materially affecting convergence.

fits_no_version.finding: Three-layer polynomial networks with fixed random features fit original and random MNIST labels to low regression loss after projection to 100 PCA dimensions and input perturbation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A polynomial random-feature layer enables low-loss memorization of perturbed, dimension-reduced MNIST targets.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorems 4–6 guarantee arbitrarily small squared training loss using perturbed gradient descent under specified feature-rank, width and boundedness conditions, with smoothed-input and deterministic-rank variants.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Appropriately constructed mildly overparameterized polynomial networks admit efficient memorization guarantees under explicit data conditions.

record.problems: Experiments are synthetic and MNIST regression rather than CIFAR classification; plotted outcomes generally lack exact numerical values in the text. The theoretical results require polynomial activations, data rank/general-position conditions, and perturbed gradient descent; the MNIST experiments use Adam and input perturbations.
record.rows_left_out: No rows left out. Figure-only numeric values were not reconstructed; accompanying textual descriptions were recorded where available.

untested.parts: Convolutional networks trained from random initialization on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100; training classification error with original, corrupted or random labels; and the effects of model size, early stopping and regularization.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, frequencies of spurious local minima as widths grow together, and adding one or two student neurons.
Depth-dependent training degradation in plain convolutional networks and its prevention by identity shortcuts or special initialization.
Comparisons of activation-matched initializations, signal and gradient propagation, training speed, and trainable depth.
Learning rates relative to the initial stability threshold, transient loss growth and curvature reduction, divergence, and long-term edge-of-stability dynamics.
Batch normalization comparisons for accuracy gain, learning-rate tolerance and training stability, including comparisons with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: States are cannot_determine relative to the supplied versions because all rows are linked to none; this does not dispute the reported regression outcomes. Citations to Zhang et al. and Safran and Shamir do not constitute tests of V1 or V2. The omitted theoretical guarantees fit no supplied version, so they are recorded under fits_no_version rather than missing.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100 classification error, convolutional networks, SGD, or smaller models/early stopping/regularized recipes as described in the version. Tests synthetic and MNIST regression with squared loss, including random labels.

rows.subject: two-layer network with quadratic activation (synthetic example)
rows.stage_stated: random initialization (algorithm initialized at W=0); trained with gradient descent
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent on squared loss to fit random synthetic samples and labels
rows.note: Text explicitly describes the loss outcome; no numerical final loss is stated.
rows.check: Zero synthetic regression loss does not measure any supplied version. The initialization description is inconsistent: W=0 is deterministic, and Theorem 4 uses perturbed gradient descent from zero; the experiment reports simple gradient descent without explicitly documenting its initialization.

rows.subject: two-layer network with quadratic activation (MNIST original labels)
rows.operation_detail: Adam training on original MNIST inputs and labels using squared loss

conditions.value: decay by a factor of 0.3 every 15 epochs

rows.value: loss decreases to a small value (∼ 0.1), but the decrease becomes slower afterwards
rows.note: Authors attribute the slowdown as likely due to small singular values in the input feature matrix.
rows.check: The approximately 0.1 value is squared regression loss for scalar MNIST labels, not CIFAR classification error in a convolutional network. Random initialization is not explicitly specified for this experiment.
